pqc.menuDesc: Keys that stay private even after secp256k1 is broken
pqc.reasonShortSeed: This account uses a {count}-word seed phrase. Post-quantum keys must come from a 24-word phrase — a shorter one carries only 128 bits of entropy, which would become the weakest link.
pqc.reason.read-only: This is a watch-only account. It has no private key, so it cannot hold post-quantum keys.
pqc.reason.remote-signer: This account signs through a remote signer, and that protocol has no post-quantum operations yet.
pqc.reason.no-seed: This account was imported from a private key, so there is no seed phrase to derive from.
pqc.independentHint: You can still add a standalone post-quantum key using the pqc:keygen command. It is not recoverable from a seed phrase, so you must back it up separately.
pqc.readyDesc: Your keys are derived from your 24-word seed phrase. Nothing extra to back up — the words you already wrote down restore them.
pqc.publishDesc: Publish this event to your relays so others can send you post-quantum encrypted messages. Until you do, senders fall back to classic encryption.
pqc.limits: This protects the confidentiality of messages sent from now on, permanently. It does not stop a quantum attacker from forging events in your name — that needs a signature migration, which is not part of this.
pqc.cardDesc: Messages sent to you stay private even after today's cryptography is broken
pqc.published: Published to {sent} of {relays} relays. People can now send you post-quantum messages.
pqc.alreadyPublished: Your post-quantum keys are already published and up to date.
pqc.staleAttestation: Your published keys no longer match this account. Publish again so senders use the right key.
pqc.importDesc: You can generate a standalone post-quantum key on your own machine and import it here. Nothing is sent anywhere — the generator runs offline, and you can read its source before running it.
pqc.importPaste: Paste the key file, or choose it below
pqc.importedBackupWarning: This key is not recoverable from your seed phrase. If you lose your copy of the key file, messages sent to it can never be read again.
pqc.importRemoveConfirm: Remove this key? Anyone who already has your attestation will keep encrypting to it, and you will no longer be able to read those messages.
pqc.importFileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
